entities.name: Hydrocarbon exposure
observations: Automotive-related hydrocarbon ingestion can cause aspiration and chemical pneumonitis; emesis, gastric lavage, and routine activated charcoal increase aspiration risk.
Unknown hydrocarbon products may warrant ECG assessment for cardiac toxicity or co-ingestants.

entities.name: Chemical pneumonitis
observations: Symptomatic children with cough and radiographic opacities after hydrocarbon ingestion require hospital observation, serial respiratory assessment, and supportive care.
Routine antibiotics, bronchoscopy, and endoscopy are not indicated without bacterial infection, airway obstruction, severe persistent respiratory failure, or suspected caustic injury.

entities.name: ECG in unknown hydrocarbon ingestion
observations: With an unknown automotive-related product, ECG is an appropriate focused test to assess possible cardiac effects or additives/co-ingestants; it should not delay respiratory support.
